swap_risks: HIGH TEMPERATURE GRADE MISMATCH: Rated ambient range differs (LM2903DR: -40..125 °C Extended Industrial (-40°C to 125°C) vs LM393DR: 0..70 °C Commercial (0°C to 70°C)); LM393DR cold limit only 0 °C, LM393DR hot limit only 70 °C — verify product ambient qualification before swapping.
BENCH VERIFICATION: Confirm thermal dissipation margin using θJA (LM2903DR: 148.5 °C/W vs LM393DR: 148.5 °C/W) and worst-case ambient temperature (-40..125 °C vs 0..70 °C).
engineering_verdict: LM2903DR (Texas Instruments, SOIC-8) and LM393DR (Texas Instruments, SOIC-8) are Level 2 Functional / Tuning Required alternatives: the PCB land pattern is compatible, but passive retuning or rating derating is mandatory because ambient temperature grade differs (-40..125 °C vs 0..70 °C). Signal-chain deltas: propagation delay 1300 ns (p.10) vs 1300 ns (p.10), supply ceiling 30 V (p.4) vs 30 V (p.4), Vos 7 mV (p.10) vs 5 mV (p.8), Ib 1x gap (25000 vs 25000 pA). Primary bench gotchas to watch: LM2903DR "Extended -40°C to +125°C Upgrade Over LM393DR, But Wider Offset (7 mV / 15 mV Over Temp)" (p.10) and LM393DR "Classic LM358DR / LMV358IDR Identical SOIC-8 Pinout Trap (Missing Pull-Up & Oscillation)" (p.3). BOM decision: Choose LM2903DR when matching your existing Texas Instruments SOIC-8 (D) qualification and -40..125 °C grade; choose LM393DR when ultra-low supply current (225 µA/ch) is prioritized. Always verify Pin 1 orientation (TOP_VIEW p.3 vs TOP_VIEW p.3) and official datasheets on hardware prototypes prior to production.
